summary: The exact candidate is a partial fix. It makes newline-terminated device printf output visible after torch.cuda.synchronize() in a clean process with piped or regular-file stdout, and its regression passes on the assigned MI350X. However, its import-time setvbuf(stdout, ...) is performed after stdout may already have been used. An independent GPU counterexample wrote one C-stdio record before importing FlyDSL; the candidate flushed that record, but all four later device printf lines remained buffered after synchronization and appeared only at process teardown. This violates the original broad piped/redirected-output contract and is especially relevant to long-lived notebook kernels.

tests.what_was_measured: Original failure reproduced: after synchronize the child was alive and READY, with 0/4 lines readable; all four lines appeared after exit.
All four candidate cases passed: one/three launches, with and without the explicit flush helper, while the child remained alive.
Independent unchanged hello(); torch.cuda.synchronize() pipe case exposed exactly four thread lines before process teardown in a clean process.

Regular-file stdout passed, but after libc printf wrote to stdout before FlyDSL import, only PREIMPORT was visible after GPU synchronization; the four device lines appeared only after child exit. The harness intentionally exited 4 for this remaining contract failure.
Fresh compilation and execution passed. LLVM IR called __ockl_printf_begin, __ockl_printf_append_string_n, and __ockl_printf_append_args; final ISA targeted amdgcn-amd-amdhsa-unknown-gfx950.
All 15 focused runtime and printf-lowering unit tests passed.
Real GPU vector addition matched the independent PyTorch a+b reference with maximum error 0.00e+00 over 1,048,576 float32 elements.

gpu_execution.evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950/capability 9.5, ran the original reproducer, candidate regression, adversarial cases, fresh printf compilation, and numerical vector-add check.

remaining_counterexamples: With piped stdout, call libc printf before importing FlyDSL, then import FlyDSL and run the unchanged device hello(); torch.cuda.synchronize() sequence. At READY while the child is alive, only the pre-import bytes are readable; all four device lines remain buffered until teardown.
remaining_limitations: The candidate was tested only on the prepared Linux/glibc 2.39 ROCm 7.2 environment with one MI350X/gfx950 GPU; no actual Jupyter frontend was available.
The candidate changes only Python files. No C++/LLVM source changed, so the prescribed native rebuild was not applicable.
Source imports resolved to /job/repo/python/flydsl. The native package remained the pinned wheel at /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/flydsl/_mlir.
The candidate changes process-wide libc stdout buffering for every C/C++ writer after FlyDSL import.

C setvbuf is only safely specified before other operations on a stream; the observed pre-import-write failure demonstrates that the import-time approach cannot cover already-active stdout streams reliably.
